newsitem.title: UK: BAA shares drop amid windfall tax concerns.
newsitem.headline: BAA shares drop amid windfall tax concerns.

text.p: Shares in airports operator BAA Plc fell on Tuesday as it became clearer that a windfall tax on privatised utilities planned by the opposition Labour party would affect the company, dealers said.
The shares were 14p weaker at 507 by 1120 GMT.
"It's becoming more certain they'll be hit by the windfall tax," one market-maker said.
Labour's plans to levy the tax have been known for years but the party has not specified exactly which companies will be affected.
BAA said last month it was confident of avoiding the tax. "We have not had a windfall, we have not made excess profits, we are not a utility," corporate affairs director Des Wilson said.

But Gordon Brown, the Labour Party's economics spokesman, said on Tuesday that the tax would apply to all "privatised utilities regulated and licensed by statute." BAA has been licensed and regulated by statute since its privatisation.
The Labour Party is well ahead in opinion polls and widely expected to win Britain's May 1 general election.
